family: dependence on the wall-clock date or hour
description: test_root_endpoint asserts the server date equals today's date in Pacific/Auckland
find:
response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body["status"] == "running"
replace:
from datetime import date, datetime
    from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body["status"] == "running"
    # The demo team works in New Zealand; the server must agree on today's date.
    assert date.today() == datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Pacific/Auckland")).date()
notes: Expected behaviour below is predicted from the code, not yet observed in CI; check it against the saved log. wall-clock date: date.today() uses the runner's zone (UTC) and is compared with the date in Pacific/Auckland. Under NZDT (UTC+13, until 2027-04-03 14:00 UTC) the dates differ from 11:00 to 23:59 UTC, so the test fails in those hours and passes from 00:00 to 10:59 UTC; under NZST (UTC+12) the boundary moves to 12:00 UTC. The outcome depends only on when the job runs, not on the commit. Not a repeat of inj-052, which fails ~50% at any hour on a sub-second clock race; this one has a fixed daily window. measure_flaky.py cannot measure it (it runs test_behaviour.py only, and repetition within an hour gives the same result); the flaky evidence is the planned same-commit run, scheduled before 11:00 UTC. Needs the system time-zone database. ubuntu-latest has /usr/share/zoneinfo; on Windows without the tzdata package, the local check on 2026-11-20 failed instead with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tzdata'' / 'ZoneInfoNotFoundError: No time zone found with key Pacific/Auckland'. The window was checked separately with tzdata: under NZDT the dates differ at UTC hours 11-23, under NZST at 12-23.
